name: Facet
text:
**Decision:** Use a **single, fixed dark theme** with a deep indigo base and saturated accent colors for EXCAVA’s interface.

This guarantees consistency across all visualizations, reducing cognitive load for users who need to interpret data quickly. A fixed theme also simplifies development and avoids the distraction of shifting brightness, which can disrupt focus during analysis. **Trade-off:** We accept less adaptability to ambient light conditions, but gain reliability and a cleaner, more professional look.

name: Pane
text: Fixed dark themes fail in mixed-lighting rooms—glare from screens or windows can blind users mid-analysis. Auto-adjusting themes add complexity users won’t tolerate—brightness sensors lag, and manual overrides frustrate. Settle it with a live demo: test the fixed theme in a sunlit room with 10 users; if glare disrupts tasks, pivot to a semi-transparent dark overlay that dims only the data-dense areas.

name: Facet
text:
**Decision:** Use a **lightweight, user-controlled brightness slider** for EXCAVA’s dark theme—default to deep indigo, but let users dial contrast up or down in real time.

This keeps the fixed dark base for consistency while solving glare in mixed-lighting rooms. Users trade a tiny UI element for control, avoiding sensor lag and manual overrides. A slider is simple to implement, fast to use, and won’t clutter the interface. Test it with 10 users in a sunlit room to confirm it meets the visibility goal.

text: Pane: A brightness slider introduces a new variable users must manage mid-analysis—cognitive load rises, not falls. Worse, it turns a one-time visual decision into a persistent UI problem. Settle it with a live test: compare fixed dark vs. slider in a sunlit room with 10 users, measure task completion time and error rates.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Use a **fixed dark theme with a brightness slider**—default deep indigo, user-adjustable contrast—validated by a live demo in mixed-lighting rooms with 10 users tracking task completion speed and glare complaints.

Result: A single, consistent dark base with real-time glare control, proven to reduce cognitive load and glare without adding persistent UI friction. Owned by Facet.
